title: Prevent false sample-volume shortages at decimal boundaries
source: lib/ohworks-sample-volume.ts:191-215 subtracts and compares raw binary floating-point volumes; tests/ohworks/sample-volume.test.ts:54-58 only covers an integer exact fit. Inline reproduction: 0.3 mL with ordered 0.1 and 0.2 mL draws incorrectly marks CBC short by 2.7755575615628914e-17 mL. Planning verification on ef1f4da1633e6d4e90348ea613055691f1131580: the eight assigned existing test files passed 291/291 tests using TSX_DISABLE_CACHE=1 node --import /private/tmp/actorlab-654-review-base/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs --test followed by their exact paths (read-only existing loader; no dependency installation). All eight defect reproductions were separately asserted inline against unchanged source. Held backlog and live GitHub issues #72, #94, #95 were read on 2026-10-07; all remain open. #72 requires cross-repository reconciliation; #94 requires production configuration and external-inbox proof; #95 requires OAuth operations. prompt:
Fix the decimal boundary error in the synthetic sample-volume allocator. In lib/ohworks-sample-volume.ts:191-215, subtraction leaves binary floating-point residue and the strict sufficiency comparison mistakes that residue for a real shortage. A reproduced request with specimenVolumeMl=0.3, containerDeadVolumeMl=0, GLUCOSE requiring 0.1 at sequence 0, and CBC requiring 0.2 at sequence 1, both routine, incorrectly marks CBC short by 2.7755575615628914e-17 mL. The integer exact-fit test at tests/ohworks/sample-volume.test.ts:54-58 does not exercise this case.

Keep the change inside this allocator. Introduce a narrowly bounded, scale-aware floating-point comparison tolerance and clamp only roundoff-sized negative remainders to zero. Do not use a broad fixed epsilon that could authorize a meaningful overdraft, especially for very small volumes. Preserve priority ordering, deterministic tie breaking, and the rule that a short test consumes no volume.

Extend tests/ohworks/sample-volume.test.ts with the reproduced decimal sequence, decimal dead-volume subtraction, a genuinely insufficient nearby amount, and a very small positive requirement with zero supply. Assert runnable codes and nonnegative remaining volumes, not just absence of errors. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks/sample-volume.test.ts. Use synthetic fixtures only. work on the assigned branch you are on. Edit only the two allowed files; no merges, rebases, commits, pushes, or external operations.
